rsu-tax.title: Separate wage value from retained shares equivalent
rsu-tax.inputs: settlement: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; fmv: 50; method: 2026 optional supplemental method; prior_supplemental: 0; actual_federal: 1100; other_withholding: 400; assumed_federal_rate: 32
steps: 100 × 50 = 5,000 taxable wage value.
Optional federal withholding at 22% is 1,100. Add the entered 400 other withholding.
Retained value = 5,000 − 1,500 = 3,500; 3,500 / 50 = 70 shares equivalent. This is not broker rounding.
rsu-tax.answer: Value after allocated withholding: 3,500.00 for the stated assumptions.

rsu-tax.title: Split an award across the $1 million supplemental threshold
rsu-tax.inputs: settlement: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; fmv: 50; method: 2026 optional supplemental method; prior_supplemental: 998000; actual_federal: 1100; other_withholding: 400; assumed_federal_rate: 32
steps: Prior supplemental wages are 998,000, leaving 2,000 within the 22% band.
Current award withholding = 2,000 × 22% + 3,000 × 37% = 1,550.
The assumed federal tax at 32% is 1,600, only 50 above this federal withholding; that difference is a scenario, not a return.
rsu-tax.answer: Federal income tax withheld: 1,550.00 for the stated assumptions.

rsu-tax.title: Enter actual federal withholding instead of assuming a payroll method
rsu-tax.inputs: settlement: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; fmv: 50; method: Enter actual federal withholding; prior_supplemental: 0; actual_federal: 1500; other_withholding: 400; assumed_federal_rate: 32
steps: Use the supplied actual federal amount 1,500, rather than the optional 22% method.
With 400 other withholding, retained value is 5,000 − 1,900 = 3,100.
rsu-tax.answer: Value after allocated withholding: 3,100.00 for the stated assumptions.

rsu-tax.title: Sell an already-taxed known lot without double counting wage income
rsu-tax.inputs: acquired: 2026-01-15; sold: 2026-11-24; sold_shares: 70; income_fmv: 50; sale_price: 80; fees: 10; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15
steps: Only 70 shares are sold. Income-date basis = 70 × 50 = 3,500.
Gross proceeds = 70 × 80 = 5,600; after 10 fees, net proceeds = 5,590.
Capital gain = 5,590 − 3,500 = 2,090. Wage income recognized previously is not charged again.
rsu-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss on sold shares: 2,090.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss on sold shares

rsu-tax.title: Preserve a later stock loss without promising a tax refund
rsu-tax.inputs: acquired: 2026-01-15; sold: 2026-11-24; sold_shares: 70; income_fmv: 50; sale_price: 40; fees: 10; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15
steps: Net sale proceeds = 70 × 40 − 10 = 2,790.
Basis remains 3,500; capital loss is −710.
This worksheet gives no automatic tax benefit for that loss.
rsu-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss on sold shares: -710.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss on sold shares

rsu-tax.title: Use the entered long-term rate after the acquisition anniversary
rsu-tax.inputs: acquired: 2024-11-23; sold: 2026-11-24; sold_shares: 70; income_fmv: 50; sale_price: 80; fees: 10; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15
steps: The nonrestricted share acquisition date is more than a year before the 2026 sale.
The 2,090 gain uses the entered 15% long-term assumption, giving 313.50.
This is not a calculation of the filer’s actual capital-gain bracket or NIIT.
rsu-tax.answer: Assumed capital-gain tax on positive gain: 313.50 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Assumed capital-gain tax on positive gain

espp-tax.title: Keep the lookback purchase price distinct from the grant-date price
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2023-12-01; purchase: 2024-06-01; sale: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 100; purchase_fmv: 80; sale_price: 120; fees: 10; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 68; grant_option: 85
steps: Actual price is 68, while grant-date as-if exercise price is 85 against grant FMV 100.
Qualifying compensation per share = min(100 − 85, 120 − 68) = 15. For 100 shares this is 1,500.
Basis = 6,800 + 1,500 = 8,300. Net proceeds 11,990 less basis gives 3,690 capital gain.
espp-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis: 3,690.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis

espp-tax.title: Derive the same prices from a 15% lower-FMV lookback
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2023-12-01; purchase: 2024-06-01; sale: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 100; purchase_fmv: 80; sale_price: 120; fees: 10; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; discount: 15; price_base: Lower of grant / purchase FMV
steps: Actual purchase price = min(100, 80) × 85% = 68.
Grant-date as-if option price = 100 × 85% = 85. These are not interchangeable.
The resulting compensation and basis match the actual-price example.
espp-tax.answer: Actual purchase price per share used: 68.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Actual purchase price per share used

espp-tax.title: Retain compensation and a capital loss in an early declining sale
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2025-12-01; purchase: 2026-06-01; sale: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 100; purchase_fmv: 80; sale_price: 60; fees: 10; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 68; grant_option: 85
steps: The date test is disqualifying. Purchase spread = 80 − 68 = 12 per share, so compensation is 1,200.
Adjusted basis is 6,800 + 1,200 = 8,000. Net proceeds are 5,990.
Capital loss = 5,990 − 8,000 = −2,010, while economic loss is only 810. No automatic capital-loss tax offset is applied.
espp-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis: -2,010.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis

espp-tax.title: Distinguish a disqualifying sale from short-term capital gain
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2025-01-01; purchase: 2025-06-01; sale: 2026-07-01; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 100; purchase_fmv: 80; sale_price: 120; fees: 10; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 68; grant_option: 85
steps: The two-year grant period is not complete, but the purchase holding period exceeds one year.
Compensation is 1,200; adjusted basis is 8,000. Net proceeds 11,990 give 3,990 long-term capital gain.
Disqualifying disposition does not automatically mean all income is short-term capital gain.
espp-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis: 3,990.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis

espp-tax.title: Preserve a qualifying-date loss with zero compensation
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2023-12-01; purchase: 2024-06-01; sale: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 100; purchase_fmv: 80; sale_price: 60; fees: 10; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 68; grant_option: 85
steps: Both date periods are complete, but sale price 60 is below purchase price 68.
Compensation is zero; basis remains 6,800. Net proceeds 5,990 create an 810 capital loss.
espp-tax.answer: Ordinary compensation income at disposition: 0.00 for the stated assumptions.

espp-tax.title: Reproduce IRS Example 10 arithmetic with illustrative 2026 dates
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2023-12-01; purchase: 2025-06-01; sale: 2026-08-01; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 22; purchase_fmv: 23; sale_price: 30; fees: 0; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 20; grant_option: 20
steps: The IRS example prices are grant FMV 22, fixed option price 20, exercise FMV 23 and sale price 30.
After the required date periods, compensation is (22 − 20) × 100 = 200.
Basis is 2,000 + 200 = 2,200; sale proceeds 3,000 give 800 capital gain. Dates here are original 2026 illustrations.
espp-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis: 800.00 for the stated assumptions.

expected.label: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis

espp-tax.title: Reproduce IRS Example 11 early-sale arithmetic with 2026 dates
espp-tax.inputs: plan: Section 423 plan confirmed; grant: 2024-11-01; purchase: 2026-05-01; sale: 2026-11-24; shares: 100; grant_fmv: 22; purchase_fmv: 23; sale_price: 30; fees: 0; ordinary_rate: 32; short_rate: 32; long_rate: 15; paid: 20; grant_option: 20
steps: The purchase holding period is not complete. Compensation = (23 − 20) × 100 = 300.
Basis becomes 2,300; proceeds 3,000 produce 700 capital gain.
These are the IRS example’s amounts with original illustrative 2026 dates, not a copied taxpayer record.
espp-tax.answer: Capital gain / loss after compensation basis: 700.00 for the stated assumptions.
